scope: logical persistence authority and schema-admission policy; not full relational schema

technology_posture.replaceability_rule: Technology choices may be replaced only through the governing contract/architecture revision process; semantic meaning remains above persistence.

principles.rule: Every persisted mutable fact belongs to exactly one owning runtime module; only that module may write it.
Cross-domain repository imports, foreign-table writes, and persistence-layer ownership bypasses are forbidden.
Application code depends on owner-defined persistence ports; Infrastructure implements those ports and contains Drizzle/PostgreSQL details.

A physical schema object may be introduced only when every semantic dependency it encodes is approved: entity, identifier, required lifecycle state set, required relationship/cardinality, and any shape-affecting owner decision.
Candidate K00 semantics may be preserved in discovery metadata but may not become columns, enums, foreign keys, indexes, checks, or repository API assumptions.
Protected records require authoritative organization ownership/scope where applicable, and protected queries require scope predicates in the data-access implementation.
Browser-reachable database roles have no read/write access to backend-owned application tables; privilege/RLS posture is tested when such roles exist.
Required audit records commit atomically with security-sensitive mutations and are append-only at the persistence privilege boundary.
Idempotency identity is durably bound to operation/payload semantics when the owning contract requires idempotency; duplicate safe retry cannot create duplicate authoritative effects.
Ambiguous external effects persist reconciliation state before retry; unreadable provider state remains unresolved and forbids automatic retry.
Every shared/production schema change is represented by an immutable ordered migration; direct schema synchronization/manual DDL is forbidden outside governed migration paths.
Destructive migrations require explicit owner approval and written rollback/recovery evidence; release must reconcile migration-defined schema with deployed database state.
Retention/deletion/anonymization implementation remains blocked where C15 policy questions are unresolved; persistence must not encode a guessed purge policy.
Persistence Model approval does not authorize Transport routes, UI data contracts, physical package paths, microservices, or candidate event integration.

acceptance_targets: Static architecture test rejects Infrastructure/Repository imports across owning modules.
Static persistence-admission test rejects schema definitions that encode candidate identifiers, states, relationships, or entities.
Migration test rejects schema changes without a migration and rejects edits to already-applied migrations.
Empty-database migration replay produces deterministic schema.
Protected-query test proves authoritative scope predicate at data-access boundary.
Browser-role test denies access to every backend-owned table if a browser-reachable DB role exists.
Audit privilege test rejects UPDATE/DELETE and forced audit-write failure rolls back owning mutation.
Reconciliation persistence test proves unresolved provider readback cannot be converted into retryable success.
